theorems.name: Contract Pathwise PV is Additive Over both
theorems.description: pathPV is additive over Contract.both: the pathwise present value of two combined contracts along one fixed scenario is the sum of their pathwise present values, for any discount curve D. Purely a finite-list-sum fact about pathPV -- no integral, measure or integrability hypothesis is involved yet.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Contracts.Core

open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.Contracts

variable {ι : Type*}

/-- `pathPV` is additive over `Contract.both`. -/
theorem pathPV_both' (D : ℝ≥0 → ℝ) (s : Scenario ι) (a b : Contract ι) :
    (Contract.both a b).pathPV D s = a.pathPV D s + b.pathPV D s :=
  MathFin.Contracts.Contract.pathPV_both D s a b

theorems.name: A Payoff is Adapted to Its Observation Times
theorems.description: Evaluating a Payoff against a filtration-adapted model X is F_u-measurable as soon as every observation time the payoff's syntax reads is <= u -- the adaptedness hypothesis a Payoff needs to be a legitimate pricing integrand. obsTimes is a syntactic over-approximation, so the theorem gives a sufficient, not necessary, adaptedness criterion.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Contracts.Adapted

open MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.Contracts

variable {ι Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}

/-- Evaluating a payoff against a filtration-adapted model is `𝓕 u`-measurable
once every observation time it reads is `≤ u`. -/
theorem measurable_eval_of_obsTimes_le' {𝓕 : Filtration ℝ≥0 mΩ} {u : ℝ≥0}
    (e : Payoff ι) (X : ι → ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ)
    (hX : ∀ i t, Measurable[𝓕 t] (X i t))
    (hle : ∀ t ∈ e.obsTimes, t ≤ u) :
    Measurable[𝓕 u] fun ω ↦ e.eval (fun i t ↦ X i t ω) :=
  MathFin.Contracts.Payoff.measurable_eval_of_obsTimes_le e X hX hle

theorems.name: Contract Value is Additive Over both
theorems.description: Contract.value is additive over Contract.both, given both summands' discounted pathwise present values are Q-integrable: the value of a combined contract is the sum of the two values. Unlike value_scale (unconditional, since integral_const_mul holds even off the integrable set), this direction genuinely needs both integrability hypotheses -- integral_add is false without them.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Contracts.Pricing

open MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.Contracts

variable {ι Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}

/-- `Contract.value` is additive over `both`, given both summands' discounted
pathwise present values are integrable. -/
theorem value_both' (Q : Measure Ω) (D : ℝ≥0 → ℝ)
    (X : ι → ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ) (a b : Contract ι)
    (ha : Integrable (fun ω ↦ a.pathPV D (scenarioAt X ω)) Q)
    (hb : Integrable (fun ω ↦ b.pathPV D (scenarioAt X ω)) Q) :
    (Contract.both a b).value Q D X = a.value Q D X + b.value Q D X :=
  MathFin.Contracts.Contract.value_both Q D X a b ha hb

theorems.name: Value of Delivering a Martingale Asset
theorems.description: A contract that simply delivers a Q-martingale asset S at time T, undiscounted, is worth today's Q-expectation of S at time 0: value = integral S_0 dQ. Proved from Martingale.condExp_ae_eq chained through integral_condExp; needs only that S is a Q-martingale and Q a probability measure, no equivalent-martingale-measure (IsEMM) content.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Contracts.Pricing

open MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.Contracts

variable {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}

/-- A contract that simply delivers a `Q`-martingale asset `S` at `T`,
undiscounted, is worth today's `Q`-expectation of `S` at time `0`. -/
theorem value_deliverAsset' {𝓕 : Filtration ℝ≥0 mΩ}
    {S : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} {Q : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
    (hM : Martingale S 𝓕 Q) (T : ℝ≥0) :
    (Contract.pay T (Payoff.obs () T)).value Q (fun _ ↦ 1) (fun _ ↦ S)
      = ∫ ω, S 0 ω ∂Q :=
  MathFin.Contracts.Contract.value_deliverAsset hM T

metadata.reference: Risk-neutral pricing of asset delivery (Shreve 5.2, martingale pricing). Contract-reification framing after P. Bilokon, The Contract Is Not the Model (working paper, 2026), github.com/thalesians/lean_contracts (Apache-2.0); no code copied.

The contract observes and pays the asset only at the single time T (Contract.pay T (Payoff.obs () T)); the discount curve is fixed to the constant 1 (undiscounted) and the model to a single asset (fun _ => S). Hypotheses are Martingale S 𝓕 Q and [IsProbabilityMeasure Q] -- deliberately not the library's IsEMM bundle, since this argument never touches the mutual-absolute-continuity content (ac/ac') that distinguishes an equivalent martingale measure from a bare martingale measure. theorems.name: Reified European Call Prices to the Black-Scholes Formula
theorems.description: The reified European call contract europeanCall K T -- a Payoff literally built from max, sub, obs and const nodes rather than an inline lambda -- prices under the single-asset Black-Scholes model to the closed-form call formula S_0 Phi(d_1) - K e^{-rT} Phi(d_2). The proof reduces Contract.value to the exact integral MathFin.bs_call_formula already computes; no new Black-Scholes content is proved here.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Contracts.Models.BlackScholes

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.Contracts

variable {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}

/-- The reified European call prices to the Black-Scholes call formula. -/
theorem value_europeanCall' {Q : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
    {S_0 K r σ : ℝ} {T : ℝ≥0} {Z : Ω → ℝ} (h : BSCallHyp Q S_0 K r σ T Z) :
    (europeanCall K T).value Q (fun _ ↦ Real.exp (-r * T)) (bsAssets S_0 r σ T Z)
      = S_0 * Phi (bsd1 S_0 K r σ T) - K * Real.exp (-r * T) * Phi (bsd2 S_0 K r σ T) :=
  MathFin.Contracts.value_europeanCall h

metadata.reference: Black-Scholes European call formula (Hull 15.6, Shreve 4.5). Contract-reification framing after P. Bilokon, The Contract Is Not the Model (working paper, 2026), github.com/thalesians/lean_contracts (Apache-2.0); no code copied.

theorems.name: Capped Call as a Composed Contract
theorems.description: The composed contract cappedCall K1 K2 T -- a long call at K1 plus a short call at K2 -- really pays min(max(S_T - K1, 0), K2 - K1) in every scenario. This payoff identity is what earns the composed object its name; the contract's Black-Scholes value is a separate theorem, published as mf-contract-capped-call-value.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Contracts.Instruments.Options

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.Contracts

variable {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}

/-- The composed contract really pays the capped-call payoff. -/
theorem cappedCall_payoff_eq' {K₁ K₂ : ℝ} (h : K₁ ≤ K₂) {T : ℝ≥0}
    (s : Scenario Unit) :
    (cappedCall K₁ K₂ T).pathPV (fun _ ↦ 1) s
      = min (max (s () T - K₁) 0) (K₂ - K₁) :=
  MathFin.Contracts.cappedCall_payoff_eq h s

theorems.name: Capped Call Value by Composition
theorems.description: The capped call's Black-Scholes value -- the price of cappedCall K1 K2 T under the single-asset Black-Scholes model -- is the difference of the two europeanCall closed forms, obtained by Contract.value_both and Contract.value_scale applied to value_europeanCall twice: composition, not a third integral, produces the price. The integrability hypotheses Contract.value_both would otherwise need are discharged internally (domination against the terminal asset price's Gaussian MGF), not left for the caller to supply.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Contracts.Models.BlackScholes

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin MathFin.Contracts

variable {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}

/-- The capped call's Black-Scholes value is the difference of the two European
call values, by composition -- no integral is touched a third time. -/
theorem value_cappedCall' {Q : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
    {S_0 K₁ K₂ r σ : ℝ} {T : ℝ≥0} {Z : Ω → ℝ}
    (h₁ : BSCallHyp Q S_0 K₁ r σ T Z) (h₂ : BSCallHyp Q S_0 K₂ r σ T Z) :
    (cappedCall K₁ K₂ T).value Q (fun _ ↦ Real.exp (-r * T)) (bsAssets S_0 r σ T Z)
      = (S_0 * Phi (bsd1 S_0 K₁ r σ T) - K₁ * Real.exp (-r * T) * Phi (bsd2 S_0 K₁ r σ T))
      - (S_0 * Phi (bsd1 S_0 K₂ r σ T) - K₂ * Real.exp (-r * T) * Phi (bsd2 S_0 K₂ r σ T)) :=
  MathFin.Contracts.value_cappedCall h₁ h₂
